camera: Straight top-down (bird's-eye) view, ship's nose pointing up toward the top of the frame, centered and filling most of the frame.
style: Detailed 16-bit-era pixel art, in the style of classic top-down shoot-'em-up sprites (Ikaruga, Raiden). Crisp hard-edged shapes, no soft gradients or airbrushed shading — use simple banded/dithered shading for depth instead. Limited, deliberate color palette (roughly 8-16 colors per ship). Strong, clean, iconic silhouette that reads instantly even at small size.
palette: Exact colors vary per ship/faction — always specified in the asset description below, not fixed here. Keep each faction's colors saturated and high-contrast against the dark background.
background: NO BACKGROUND AT ALL. Fully transparent behind and around the ship — the sprite is dropped straight onto the playfield, which the game draws itself in the sector's own colours. No tile, no panel, no card, no radial gradient, no vignette, no glow halo, no drop shadow: nothing but the ship, cut out to its silhouette.
constraints: Square 1:1 composition. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no UI elements, no drop shadow outside the subject.
_backgroundNote: This asked for a radial gradient from dark navy (#2f3b52) to near-black, and every sprite generated through generate-game-asset.yml duly baked one in — eighteen of the game's fifty-three icons, ten of them ships that draw on the board, each one a picture of a ship sitting on a dark tile sitting on a hex. A sprite carries no background. The dark field behind the fleet is the BOARD, and the renderer owns it.
wreckRule: A WRECK is the same hull as its live sprite, destroyed — not a generic pile of debris. Draw the SAME silhouette, the same hull plating and the same faction colours as that ship's own icon, so the class is still recognisable at hex size: a Hauler's wreck is a broken Hauler. Then break it: the hull cracked open along one or two lines with the interior showing, one or two pieces snapped off and drifting a few pixels clear of the main mass, panels torn back, thrusters and any lit window DEAD (no glow, no engine light, nothing emissive), and every colour knocked down toward grey — roughly half the saturation and two thirds the brightness of the live hull, keeping the faction hue just readable. No fire, no smoke, no explosion, no sparks, no debris cloud: this is cold wreckage adrift, not the moment it died. Same camera and same frame as the live sprite, and it must still read as a single object at 40 pixels across.
_wreckNote: Twenty-two of these, one per hostile class, generated separately through generate-game-asset.yml the same way the live icons were. Separate generations drift, and the answer here is this rule plus lockedPalette rather than a sheet: a sheet is for ANIMATION frames of one subject, where drift between frames is visible side by side in motion. These never appear together, and each one has to match its own live sprite rather than match the other twenty-one.
